meta.title: Rural broadband and telecom, 19 days of posts
meta.subject: broadband and rural telecommunications policy in Texas — the BEAD program and the Broadband Development Office, the Texas Universal Service Fund and its funding, rural telephone cooperatives and small carriers, pole attachment and right-of-way rules, satellite versus fiber, and who gets connected
meta.subtitle: Oct 1 to Oct 19, 2026. Each dot is one post with 1K+ views about Texas rural broadband and telecom, plus every post repeating an earlier one, in the lane for what it argues. Higher and bigger means more views. White means 90% or more the same words as an earlier post, with a white line back to it. Coloured lines link a post to the post it quoted or replied to. Updated daily.

lanes.label: Satellite connects remote Texas
lanes.description: Satellite and direct-to-phone service (Starlink, AST SpaceMobile) is the fast, practical way to reach rural and remote areas that wires and towers never will.

lanes.label: Texas builds the connectivity
lanes.description: Texas, especially Midland and the Permian Basin, is becoming the manufacturing and launch hub for satellite connectivity, bringing jobs and local economic development.

lanes.label: Spectrum and FCC open competition
lanes.description: FCC approvals, spectrum access and waived carrier-lease rules let satellite operators compete head-on with terrestrial carriers, which would lower prices and improve service.

lanes.label: Fiber is the lasting fix
lanes.description: Fiber is the durable, future-proof investment, and public money should build it to rural homes rather than rely on satellite.

lanes.label: BEAD money and Texas spending
lanes.description: The way the Texas Broadband Development Office distributes federal BEAD dollars decides who gets connected, and is criticized or defended as slow, wasteful or well targeted.

lanes.label: USF and rural carriers' survival
lanes.description: The Texas Universal Service Fund, who pays into it, and rural telephone cooperatives and small carriers' reliance on it determine whether rural service stays affordable.

lanes.label: Pushback
lanes.description: Posts doubting, mocking, fact-checking or arguing against the dominant framings.

$ASTS: 🚨🇨🇦 TELUS AND AST SPACEMOBILE SUCCESSFULLY COMPLETE FIRST SATELLITE-TO-SMARTPHONE INTEGRATION TEST ON TELUS NETWORK

Successful integration brings TELUS and AST SpaceMobile closer to connecting smartphones in remote areas of Canada where traditional cell service isn't available

VANCOUVER, BC and MIDLAND, Texas, Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TELUS and AST SpaceMobile, Inc. ("AST SpaceMobile") have successfully completed their first integration test between TELUS' wireless network and AST SpaceMobile's space-based network, marking a significant milestone in the ability to access broadband data services, make voice calls, and send text messages directly between smartphones and satellites. By combining AST SpaceMobile's innovative satellite constellation, featuring the largest communication arrays ever deployed in Low Earth Orbit (LEO), with TELUS' award-winning wireless network, Canadians will have access to a new layer of cellular broadband coverage, extending service to more places, enhancing access to critical emergency services, and bringing Canadians greater peace of mind.

"Connecting smartphones directly to satellites is opening up new possibilities for how Canadians stay connected," said Nazim Benhadid, Executive Vice-President and Chief Technology Officer, TELUS. "This successful milestone with AST SpaceMobile is a major step forward in extending cellular coverage to places where service isn't available today, reinforcing our commitment to bringing reliable service to more Canadians, no matter where they are."

How satellite technology can connect smartphones

Expected to be available to TELUS customers within the next year, this groundbreaking space-based technology will allow customers to use eligible smartphones beyond the reach of traditional cell towers, helping close existing coverage gaps across Canada and creating a future where connectivity is available virtually anywhere, by:

➡️Keeping Canadians connected in more places – whether they're travelling along busy highways, hiking, camping, exploring Canada's national parks and wilderness areas, or venturing into remote parts of the country.

➡️Expanding access to emergency services – providing another way for Canadians to reach 9-1-1, offering greater peace of mind when they need it most.

➡️Supporting workers in remote and northern communities – giving Canadians in natural resources, energy, construction and forestry a reliable way to communicate with their teams and families while working in remote areas.

➡️Bringing satellite connectivity directly to smartphones – allowing customers to stay connected using space-based cellular broadband on the smartphone they already own, with no special equipment required.

"This milestone demonstrates how mobile network operators can seamlessly extend their existing networks with space-based cellular broadband using everyday smartphones and reflects the strength and maturity of our technology," said Chris Ivory, Chief Commercial Officer at AST SpaceMobile. "Together with TELUS, we are building a new layer of connectivity that enhances network reach and resilience, helping ensure Canadians stay connected in more places across the country."

Expanding the reach of TELUS' wireless network

This partnership builds on TELUS' ongoing investments in Canada's most awarded wireless network, including faster 5G+ and LTE speeds, stronger signals and expanded coverage in communities across the country. The integration of satellite technology will complement TELUS' existing network infrastructure and further extend the reach of wireless service across Canada.

Full PR: https://t.co/q49SBQ7dNn

posts.name: Peter LINDM🅰️RK
posts.text:
$ASTS | @AST_SpaceMobile | Midland | John Joyce

Dan McCown, CTO & Co-Founder at NetAscendant Solutions:

《Midland doesn't just build things. It builds things that go to space.

Today I attended the Texas Space Coalition's Launch and Learn event, and would you believe that the Permian Basin's next boom might be 300 miles up?

The Texas Space Coalition was founded in 2024 by two 25-year Air Force veterans. Its goal is to connect industry, academia and government so that West Texas talent from UTPB, Midland College and UTEP doesn't have to move to Houston or El Segundo to work in aerospace.

Sara Harris of the Midland Development Corporation walked through the West Texas Aerospace Corridor and even the plans for a vertical orbital launch site west of Midland.

Then John Joyce, VP of Production at AST SpaceMobile, showed what's already being built here:

1. Next-gen BlueBird satellites with about 2,400 sq ft of surface area, orbiting at 17,000 mph
2. The first company delivering cellular broadband from space directly to ordinary phones without using native cellular capabilities
3. More than $6B raised to build the network
4. Demand for 500–700 satellites over the next 5 years, plus a major new facility (their 7th) planned near the Midland International Air & Space Port

When John was asked the question "Why Midland?" He said Midland has been a hand up for AST as it grew, and he described the spirit here as "I'm not going to lose, I'm going to win."

That's the wildcatter mentality. The grit that built the oil patch carries straight over to aerospace.

According to John, there are opportunities here for the whole region: machining, PLC programming, maintenance engineering, logistics, security and support services. He said the support-services skill sets are some of the hardest to hire for. This is where local businesses and schools should be paying attention.

Thank you to Matt Van Parys, the Texas Space Coalition and the Midland Development Corporation for bringing this group together, and to John for a candid, inspiring look at what AST SpaceMobile is building in our backyard.》

In a regulatory win, SpaceX has secured approval to launch and operate 15,000 next-gen satellites for Starlink Mobile.

In addition, the FCC issued a waiver so that SpaceX can offer wireless services through satellites without entering into a leasing agreement with a ground-based mobile operator. https://t.co/b0YH81ICeF

posts.name: TW
posts.text:
@SawyerMerritt From texting from orbit to 5G from orbit.

Starlink Mobile today: ~650 satellites, about 4 Mbps through T-Mobile.
Approved Oct 6: 15,000 satellites, up to 150 Mbps per user. Roughly 37x.

The FCC also waived the carrier-lease requirement, so that's real competition for AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile. Rural Texas dead zones are about to shrink.

posts.name: SpacBobby
posts.text:
$ASTS - AST SpaceMobile 'proud' to build satellites in Midland

Connecting the 2.2 billion people around the world who are unconnected to the internet or cellular phone service is the underlying mission of AST SpaceMobile.

The company plans to do just that by building the first and only space-based broadband network that will connect directly to standard mobile phones through a constellation of communications satellites built in Midland.

“It’s very exciting, what we’re doing,” said John Joyce, vice president of operations at AST, addressing a lunch and learn event hosted by the Midland Development Corporation and Texas Space Coalition. “This is a paradigm shift in how we communicate.”

Bringing connectivity to the unconnected will mean improvements in education, telehealth and banking for remote communities, he said. First responders will be able to communicate in times of emergency, Joyce added. Connectivity can also help travelers, including those at sea or in the air. The military can also use the communications ability to support more efficient and reliable missions.

The company already has multiple facilities at Midland International Air and Space Port. In July the company signed an economic development agreement with the Midland Development Corporation to lease a 23.1-acre tract owned by the city of Midland to construct a 400,000-square-foot building for satellite manufacturing and production. AST also agreed to create 1,600 full-time jobs with a payroll of $128 million by the end of 2036.

“Five years from now, I hope to see a massive facility at the airport. I want AST to be a primary stakeholder in Midland, and I want to see 7,000 cars in the parking lot,” he said.

The company already employs 1,800 people with a payroll of $144 million and supports 4,000 regional jobs. When the new facility opens, Joyce said AST expects to add $1 billion to Midland’s gross domestic product.

“The MDC and the city have been instrumental in getting us into new buildings and helping us expand to scale,” he said.

What drew AST to Midland was not just the available space but the entrepreneurial spirit of its residents.

Joyce said, “Midland also brings an ‘I’m not going to lose’ spirit’” that can’t be described anywhere else.

In return for Midland’s support, he said AST is helping attract new industries while expanding workforce training and development programs.

“I’m proud to be building the largest satellites and I’m proud we’re doing it in Midland with people from Midland,” he said.

posts.name: Bearlovesbull
posts.text:
🚨 GOOD NEWS $ASTS: DEUTSCHE BANK CALLS THE 10% SELLOFF MISGUIDED. $93 PRICE TARGET AND A VERY INTERESTING $19B SPECTRUM ARGUMENT.

Good morning everyone. 

Deutsche Bank has moved $ASTS to Buy with a $93 price target, following Friday's roughly 10% selloff.

$SPCX is moving closer to competing directly with traditional mobile carriers and investors saw  that as automatically bearish for AST SpaceMobile.

I don't think it's that simple. Remember, $ASTS is already building relationships with mobile operators that have every reason to protect their customer base as satellite connectivity becomes part of the telecom market.

If SpaceX wants to compete more directly with those carriers, AST could become an even more valuable partner rather than simply another competitor.

Now look at Deutsche Bank's spectrum argument. The bank reportedly values AST's Ligado spectrum rights at approximately $19B, compared with an enterprise value of roughly $23B.

Guys, that's a remarkable comparison. Deutsche is effectively assigning enormous strategic value to the spectrum position alone, before considering the full commercial opportunity from AST's satellite network.

Of course, that $19B is an analyst valuation, not cash sitting on AST's balance sheet. The rights still need to translate into usable capacity and commercial economics.

And there is another development I would connect with this. BlueBird 14, 15 and 16 have reportedly arrived at Cape Canaveral, while the Texas factory continues building the next satellites.

That is what I have been wanting to see from ASTS. Completed hardware moving toward launches while production continues behind it.

If AST can establish a consistent manufacturing and launch schedule, operators have a much stronger reason to commit commercially because network capacity starts becoming more predictable.

SpaceX's deeper move into telecom could actually increase the strategic value of $ASTS to established carriers.

I want to see the evidence in satellite deployments, commercial coverage, carrier commitments and eventually revenue.

I am bullish on $ASTS. I think the market is still underestimating how valuable an independent satellite broadband partner will become to mobile operators facing direct competition from SpaceX.

posts.name: ASTS Investors 🅰️
posts.text:
MIDLAND, Texas--(BUSINESS WIRE)--AST SpaceMobile, Inc. (“AST SpaceMobile”) (NASDAQ: ASTS), the company building the first and only space-based cellular broadband network accessible directly by everyday smartphones, designed for both commercial and government applications, welcomes the Letter of Intent signed by its mobile network operator partners Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefónica and Vodafone to explore a potential joint bid for Mobile Satellite Services (MSS) spectrum as AST SpaceMobile continues to advance service readiness across Europe.

The collaboration among Europe’s four largest mobile network operators is expected to accelerate network integration, improve the customer experience and extend coverage into areas without reliable mobile connectivity. The initiative supports a coordinated approach to spectrum access and service deployment, strengthening European digital data sovereignty while enabling operators to deliver space-based cellular broadband through their existing mobile services.

“Europe’s mobile network operators are taking an important step toward extending connectivity to every subscriber, wherever they live, work and travel,” said Wayne Thorsen, Chief Commercial Officer of AST SpaceMobile. “Our role is to support our partners with the satellite technology, spectrum capabilities and ground infrastructure needed to deliver cellular broadband directly to the phones people already use. Together, we are building a third layer of connectivity that expands coverage and strengthens the resilience of Europe’s mobile networks.”

AST SpaceMobile’s existing European joint venture, Satellite Connect Europe, AST SpaceMobile is providing a dedicated network of European-operated ground infrastructure that link its BlueBird satellites with mobile operators’ core networks. This infrastructure is designed to support coverage across Europe, a market with over 500 million mobile subscribers, while keeping data handling and service control within European jurisdiction. Operators retain their customer relationships as satellite connectivity extends the reach of their terrestrial networks.

AST SpaceMobile’s BlueBird satellites feature the largest communication satellites ever deployed in low Earth orbit and connect directly to standard, unmodified smartphones, backed by 3,900 patent and patent pending claims. The company has demonstrated peak download speeds of 98.9 Mbps, with next-generation satellites expected to deliver peak data rates approaching 200 Mbps. These capabilities are designed to support voice, video and broadband services for consumers, businesses, first responders and governments.

The Company’s satellite technology can tune across approximately 1,150 MHz of mobile network operator partners’ low- and mid-band spectrum globally. Together with AST SpaceMobile’s S-band priority rights, this flexibility enables the Company to combine participating operators’ spectrum with satellite spectrum to support expanded coverage and capacity in European markets, subject to applicable authorizations.

$ASTS
